Description: After squashing branches with children, use --skip-commits to cascade cleanly without conflicts
Code_Example:
# 1. Squash parent branch
git checkout LS-23/parent
git rebase -i main  # Squash to 1 commit

# 2. Identify removed commits
git checkout LS-24/child
git log --oneline LS-23/parent..HEAD
# Shows: def5678 (LS-24) + old LS-23 commits (abc1234, etc)

# 3. Create skip-commits file
@"
abc1234  # Old LS-23 commit removed during squash
"@ | Out-File skip-commits.txt

# 4. Rebase tree with skip-commits
.\scripts\rebase-branch-tree.ps1 -SkipCommitsFile skip-commits.txt

# Result: All branches stay at [+1], no conflicts!

Description: Never cascade after squashing without using skip-commits. This causes conflicts and requires re-squashing
Code_Example:
# ❌ BAD: Cascade after squash (causes conflicts)
git rebase -i main  # Squash LS-23
twig cascade  # Conflicts in all children!
# Result: Children now have [+2] commits, need re-squashing

# ✅ GOOD: Use skip-commits after squash
git rebase -i main  # Squash LS-23
# Identify removed commits: abc1234, def5678
.\scripts\rebase-branch-tree.ps1 -SkipCommits "abc1234,def5678"
# Result: All children stay [+1], no conflicts

Description: After resolving conflicts with --theirs/--ours, use skip-commits to propagate the resolution strategy rather than re-resolving
Code_Example:
# 1. Resolve conflict on parent with --theirs
git checkout LS-25/parent
# Conflict in graphql.generated.ts
git checkout --theirs apps/app/src/api/db/graphql.generated.ts
git add . && git rebase --continue

# 2. Get the resolution commit hash
git log -1 --oneline  # abc1234

# 3. Skip this commit when rebasing children
.\scripts\rebase-branch-tree.ps1 -SkipCommits "abc1234"

# Children will apply --theirs automatically, no manual resolution

Description: Use git log with range syntax to identify commits that were removed from parent during squash
Code_Example:
# After squashing LS-23 from 3 commits to 1
git checkout LS-24/child-branch

# Show all commits unique to LS-24 (including old LS-23 commits)
git log --oneline LS-23/parent..HEAD

# Output:
# def5678 (LS-24) Add web UI          ← Keep this
# abc1234 (OLD LS-23) Mobile fixes    ← Skip this
# 111222 (OLD LS-23) Type safety      ← Skip this

# Old LS-23 commits (abc1234, 111222) were squashed away
# Add them to skip-commits.txt

Description: Use rebase-branch-tree.ps1 script with skip-commits for efficient tree-wide rebasing
Code_Example:
# Method 1: Inline commit list
.\scripts\rebase-branch-tree.ps1 -SkipCommits "abc1234,def5678,ghi9012"

# Method 2: File with comments (RECOMMENDED)
@"
abc1234  # Old LS-23 commit removed during squash
def5678  # Another old LS-23 commit
# Comment lines are ignored
ghi9012  # Conflict resolution commit
"@ | Out-File skip-commits.txt

.\scripts\rebase-branch-tree.ps1 -SkipCommitsFile "skip-commits.txt"

# Method 3: Via Makefile
make rebase-tree-skip SKIP_COMMITS_FILE="skip-commits.txt"

Description: After using skip-commits, verify all branches have expected commit counts
Code_Example:
# After skip-commits rebase
twig tree

# Expected output (all [+1]):
# LS-23/parent      [+1]  ← Squashed commit
# └─ LS-24/child    [+1]  ← Only child's unique work
#    └─ LS-25/...   [+1]  ← Only grandchild's work

# If you see [+2] or higher, skip-commits didn't work:
# - Verify commit hashes are correct (7-64 hex chars)
# - Check skip-commits.txt format (no typos)
# - Ensure commits were actually removed from parent

Description: Use skip-commits after any history rewriting operation: squash, interactive rebase, conflict resolution, cherry-pick
Code_Example:
# Use skip-commits after:
# ✅ Squashing branches with children
# ✅ Interactive rebase (reordering, editing commits)
# ✅ Resolving conflicts with --theirs/--ours
# ✅ Cherry-picking fixes backward
# ✅ Amending commits that children depend on

# DON'T use skip-commits for:
# ❌ Normal forward development (just cascade)
# ❌ When branches should intentionally diverge
# ❌ When no history rewriting occurred

Description: Skip-commits is the key to maintaining [+1] commits per branch throughout cascades
Code_Example:
# Traditional approach (requires re-squashing):
# 1. Squash LS-23 → [+1]
# 2. Cascade → children get conflicts → [+2] or [+3]
# 3. Re-squash all children → back to [+1]
# 4. REPEAT for every change = tedious!

# Skip-commits approach (stays clean):
# 1. Squash LS-23 → [+1]
# 2. Identify removed: abc1234, def5678
# 3. Rebase with skip-commits → children stay [+1]
# 4. Done! No re-squashing needed ever!

Description: Skip-commits file format: one hash per line, # for comments, whitespace ignored
Code_Example:
# skip-commits.txt format
abc1234  # Old LS-23 commit removed during squash
def5678  # Another removed commit

# This is a comment line - ignored
   ghi9012   # Whitespace is trimmed

# Validation rules:
# - Must be 7-64 hexadecimal characters
# - Lines starting with # are comments
# - Empty lines are ignored
# - Inline comments after hash are OK

Description: Use make rebase-tree-skip with SKIP_COMMITS or SKIP_COMMITS_FILE variables
Code_Example:
# Inline commits
make rebase-tree-skip SKIP_COMMITS="abc1234,def5678"

# From file (recommended)
make rebase-tree-skip SKIP_COMMITS_FILE="skip-commits.txt"

# Both methods call:
# .\scripts\rebase-branch-tree.ps1 -SkipCommits/-SkipCommitsFile
